evidence.text: Merge Labs signed a multiyear exclusive license for Butterfly's Poseidon ultrasound-on-chip on ~2026-09-01 (inside Q3) with upfront and milestone licensing payments, hardware purchase commitments and technology-access fees; the Q3 guide ($26-30M, embedded guided at ~$7-8M/quarter) was set on 2026-07-30 before it, and the last comparable signing quarter (Midjourney, Q4 2025) recognised $6.8M in the quarter of signing, so Q3 embedded can land above the $7-8M run-rate and lift total revenue above the ~$29M consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Embedded-driven revenue beats were bought on the print day: Q2 2026 (revenue $32.6M vs ~$28.4-29.2M consensus, embedded $10.8M) +15.07%; Q4 2025 (Midjourney $6.8M in signing quarter) +50.65%.
evidence.why_not_priced: No 8-K disclosed the deal value (no Item 1.01), so no estimate can carry it; consensus at $28.8-29.9M sits at or below the top of a guide written before the deal. If priced, consensus would sit above $30M and the stock would not have fallen ~23% from $10.02 (CEO 10b5-1 sale price 2026-10-06) to $7.74 into the print. Revenue is recognised over time by input method (10-Q), which caps how much lands in one quarter.
evidence.independence: Midjourney precedent in Q4 2025 call coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/butterfly-network-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-30/ and Q4 2025 transcript https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/02/26/butterfly-bfly-q4-2025-earnings-call-transcript/); embedded run-rate $7-8M +/- $1-2M from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/butterfly-bfly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Inference on timing, not a disclosed number.

evidence.text: Butterfly has beaten revenue consensus four straight quarters (by 1.7% to 21.8%) and beat the top of its own Q2 guide ($27-31M) by $1.6M with $32.6M, raising FY twice (117-121 to 119-123); the Q3 guide of $26-30M is below Q2's actual, a conservative pattern that points to a print above the ~$29M bar.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a habitual beater's consensus usually drifts above the guide midpoint, and here it has ($28.8-29.9M vs $28M). It is not fully priced if consensus still sits inside the guide while the last quarter cleared the top end.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001804176/000180417626000014/bfly-20260430xexx991.htm) shows $26.5M vs $26.1M consensus and the earlier FY guide $117-121M; Q2 8-K shows the raise. Same company documents.

evidence.text: International revenue fell 14% y/y to $5.0M in Q2, which management attributed in part to orders that slipped into Q3, a timing tailwind to Q3 core revenue on top of a core business that grew only 2% in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: International was a secondary line on prior prints; no print in the baseline turned on it alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was said on the call, so it is in the guide; it only adds if the slipped orders are not already inside the $26-30M range. Small for that reason.
evidence.independence: 10-Q disaggregation shows international $5.02M vs $5.84M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1804176/000180417626000027/bfly-20260630.htm). Same company, different document.

evidence.text: Since the 2026-07-30 FY guide ($119-123M) the company announced further embedded and enterprise deals that are not in it: Merge Labs (2026-09-01, ongoing licence fees and hardware purchases), Mendaera Focalist compatibility (2026-10-01, Needham values it at ~$25M over time, launching later this year), Bridge Neurotech BCI partnership with early-access and milestone payments (2026-10-06), and a long-term VCOM education alliance (2026-10-13); these support a third FY raise or a firm Q4 rather than a cut.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two FY raises in 2026 came with +50.65% (Feb, first guide plus Midjourney) and +15.07% (July raise); the April reaffirm went -2.64%.
evidence.why_not_priced: None of these deals carried a disclosed dollar value, so no consensus model can add them; the stock fell from ~$10 (2026-10-06) to $7.74 after they were announced, which is not what a priced FY raise looks like. The Merge Labs announcement itself drew a -9.5% session.
evidence.independence: Needham initiation coverage (2026-09-22) with the Mendaera ~$25M and Midjourney $300M-by-2030 estimates: https://www.webull.com/news/15622887246988288 . Shares the Merge Labs fact with finding 1 for Q3; this finding counts only its effect on Q4/FY.

evidence.text: Management promised FedRAMP certification 'in the third quarter of 2026' in the Q2 release; no certification announcement was found by 2026-10-28, so the release may report a slip on a VA/federal channel the company has been building.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a government certification.
evidence.why_not_priced: It may simply be announced in the release; absence of a press release is weak evidence, hence the small size and wide band.
evidence.independence: GovRAMP/TX-RAMP release (2026-02-10) set the 2026 FedRAMP expectation: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260210884103/en/Butterfly-Network-Achieves-GovRAMP-and-TX-RAMP-Information-Security-Cer . No independent confirmation of a slip.

evidence.text: Q3 adjusted EBITDA was guided to a $6-9M loss against $1.4M in Q2, and the guide names AI-driven supply-chain (memory) shortages and tariffs; GE HealthCare, a direct ultrasound competitor, carries ~$100M of 2026 memory-chip inflation, so the record 71% gross margin may step back and the quality of the print can disappoint even on a revenue beat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin durability was the stated reason for the -8.5% day after the Q2 beat (outside that window); Q1 2026 (-2.64%) and earlier prints sold off on persistent losses despite revenue beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: The EBITDA step-down is guided and therefore largely priced; the memory-cost transmission to Butterfly is a peer proxy the company called 'minor' so far. Filed small for both reasons.
evidence.independence: Butterfly's own Q2 release names 'AI-driven supply chain shortages' as a risk and the 10-Q notes 'increased prices of certain inventory components' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1804176/000180417626000027/bfly-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: Short interest rose 6.2% to 33.6M shares (16.2% of float, 6.2 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement while option open interest is 86% calls (put/call 0.16) and 25d skew is -1.92 (calls bid): a crowded, building short into a name whose last three beats produced +15% to +51% print-day moves.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Print-day moves of +31.86%, +50.65% and +15.07% on the last three beats with raised outlooks; short interest was ~14.5% of float at the time of the July print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not a fact against it; it adds only convexity to a beat. If shorts were not building, SI would be flat or falling into the print.
evidence.independence: Baseline options block (put/call OI 0.16, skew -1.92, sealed 2026-10-28); June settlement 28.7M / 14.5% per Benzinga (https://benzinga.com/quote/BFLY/short-interest).

evidence.text: The core (non-embedded) business grew only 2% y/y in Q2 ($21.85M vs $21.39M) after +10% in Q1, product revenue fell to $15.7M from $16.6M, ASP fell 12% and international fell 14%; if Q3 core is flat again the print rests on lumpy licence revenue, which the market has sold before.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 beat (+15.07% on the day) was given back -8.5% the next session on durability doubts; Q1 2026 core +10% with a small beat went -2.64%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deceleration is in the 10-Q, but consensus and the wire track total revenue and embedded growth; a second flat core quarter would be read as the trend rather than a blip.
evidence.independence: Q2 call summary on ASP -12% and VCOM pricing subsidy (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/butterfly-bfly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Same company, different document.

evidence.text: Hippo's own FY2026 guide leaves a large cat cushion for H2: the 10% FY cat loss ratio on roughly $480M of NEP is ~$48M, against H1 cat of $4.3M (Q1) + $8.0M (Q2, 6.7% of NEP) = $12.3M, so ~$36M (~15% cat ratio per quarter) is loaded into Q3+Q4; likewise the $62-70M adj. net income guide implies only $24-32M for H2 against $38.2M in H1 ($17.2M + $21.0M). If Q3 cat comes in at or below ~$18M, Q3 adj. NI lands near the Q1-Q2 run-rate (~$0.50+ per share) and a second FY raise is likely; the market expects at least a reaffirmation.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-29 baseline row): beat plus a raise across every guided line, +6.87%. Q1 2026: large adjusted beat with combined-ratio guide held, -6.70%. Q4 2025: -4.89%. The stock has paid for raises, not for beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: The H2 implied cat and NI arithmetic is not printed anywhere; previews quote the FY range, not the H1 vs H2 split. If the market had priced a raise, the street Q3 EPS figure would sit near the H1 run-rate rather than at $0.27 (Benzinga), which is the bottom of the guide spread across Q3 and Q4 ($0.27 + $0.64). Partly priced by the +23% run-up.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 cat $4.3M and the 13%-cat-load original guide from the Q1 release https://app.edgar.tools/filing/1828105/0001828105-26-000023/q126earningsreleasefinal.htm ; the June 2026 reinsurance renewal cut net PMLs 31-36% https://www.reinsurancene.ws/hippo-hails-2026-reinsurance-overhaul-as-structural-evolution-in-move-to-enterprise-wide-cat-program/ . Shares the Q2 release with no other finding.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 was a heavy personal-lines cat quarter in the US: Allstate booked $1.65B pre-tax cat in Q3 2026 (July $682M, August $748M, September $220M) against $558M in Q3 2025, and Travelers' Q3 cat rose to $538M from $302M on wind and hail, driven largely by late-July SCS and the 9-12 August derecho across Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky; Illinois is among the states Hippo's 10-K lists in its GWP breakdown, and Hippo's own Q3 2025 cat was -$0.3M, so the y/y loss-ratio comparison deteriorates. Sized small because Hippo's exposure is mostly ceded and the H2 cat load (finding 1) is ~15% per quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2025 (LA wildfires, $53.4M cat, 105.9% net loss ratio) printed 2025-05-07: -15.90%. Q3 2024 cat $16.1M; Q3 2025 cat ~$0 printed 2025-11-04: +5.46%. Cat surprises are the line this stock has moved most on.
evidence.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission that Hippo has not confirmed; no Hippo cat pre-announcement. If the market had priced a heavy Q3 cat hit the stock would not have run +23% into the print to a 52-week high. Counterweight: global 9M26 cat is the lowest since 2019 (Gallagher Re), and Moody's RMS says Texas hail reports were down ~70% in H1 2026, so Hippo's TX/CA-heavy homeowners book may have missed the Midwest events.
evidence.independence: Travelers Q3 2026: cat $538M vs $302M, wind and hail https://www.reinsurancene.ws/travelers-q326-net-income-rises-despite-higher-cat-losses-but-9m-cat-toll-down-considerably/ ; derecho geography https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/catastrophe/midwest-derecho-pushes-2026-us-storm-losses-past-35-billion-brokers-say-586429.aspx ; Hippo Q3 2025 cat -$0.3M https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828105/000182810525000066/quarterlyinvestorupdatet.htm . Proxy only: no Hippo number.

evidence.text: Into the print the stock has run +23.2% in 20 days to $37.91, 1.7% below a 52-week high of $39.39 set 2026-10-22, at the $38.25 consensus target (3 of 5 ratings Hold, Zacks cut to Hold 2026-10-02), with no company news since the 2026-08-27 state-expansion release; a reaffirm or modest raise is already in the price, and the 25-delta skew of +35 vol points pays for downside.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat sold -6.70% and Q4 2025 -4.89%; Q2 2026 raise bought +6.87%. A large adjusted beat without a raise has been sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; the finding is that expectations are elevated, not that they are missed. Shrunk because short interest is low (4.3 DTC, not a crowd to squeeze or to exit) and the options chain is too thin (OI 319, 37% spread) for the skew to be a strong statement.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape: run_up_20d +23.2%, pct_from_52w_high -1.74, skew +35.13 (sealed baseline). Swingtradebot 'new uptrend' 2026-10-16 https://swingtradebot.com/equities/HIPO .

evidence.text: Accelerant, which Hippo's management said would bring more than $500M of premium to Hippo next year, grew third-party direct written premium to 47% of its $1.32B Q2 2026 exchange written premium from 27% a year earlier (~+115% y/y, ~$621M vs ~$290M), reported after Hippo last spoke; supports Hippo's guided H2 GWP acceleration in the fronting platform. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: GWP raises have come with the cat-led profit raises (Q2 2026 +6.87%); no isolated GWP surprise in the history.
evidence.why_not_priced: A counterparty's number most Hippo previews will not read; but Hippo already raised FY GWP to $1.65-1.70B and named the Accelerant volume on the Q2 call, so most of it sits inside the guide.

evidence.why_not_priced: A Q4 event that falls after the quarter being reported; previews will key on Q3. If priced, the stock would not have set a 52-week high on 2026-10-22, after landfall.

Progressive's Q2 10-Q (search snippet, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000308/pgr-20260630.htm) shows advertising up 16% with new applications up only 1%, so spend can stay high while it converts less. evidence.text: The Reciprocal's Q3 should print strong capital. Q3 2026 was a benign catastrophe quarter: Texas hail reports were down ~70% in H1 2026 against the 2023-25 average (Moody's), global insured cat losses for 9M 2026 were 29% below the 10-year average, the Atlantic season was quiet through Q3, and the first hurricane landfall was 9 Oct in Florida. The Reciprocal is Texas-heavy. Q2's gross loss ratio was 38% with Q2 the 'highest weather' quarter. The Reciprocal also holds ~16.2M PRCH shares, up from ~$12.6 (late July) to $16.66 at 30 Sept, which lifts the 'surplus plus non-admitted assets' headline by roughly $60-70M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Management leads with Reciprocal surplus: it cited $412M of surplus plus non-admitted assets at Q3 2025, which fell 33% on other lines. No clean history of a surplus surprise moving the stock on its own.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: benign weather is public, and Porch-owned EBITDA is largely insulated from Reciprocal losses since the legacy captive contract ended. The value is in the surplus headline and growth capacity before the Allied Trust closing, which is said to be surplus-neutral. This is macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by Porch for Q3, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Proxy. Q3 cat data from Gallagher Re via https://www.claimsjournal.com/news/national/2026/10/21/340831.htm (2026-10-21). Reciprocal's 16.2M PRCH holding is in the Q2 exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000046/prch-20260729xexx991.htm. Prices from Yahoo daily bars.

evidence.text: On 13 Oct 2026 Porch agreed to buy Allied Trust's Texas carrier, MGA and captive reinsurer for $200M. Porch-owned HoldCo pays $95M ($75M cash + up to $20M stock) for the MGA and captive. Management guides ~$200M of added RWP and ~$25M of adj. EBITDA (ex-Reciprocal) at under 4x. Closing is not before 1 Jan 2027. The call is the first chance for a 2027 framework that includes it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On announcement the stock went $17.69 to $17.22 (13 Oct) and $16.44 (14 Oct, -7.1% over two days), then recovered to $17.57 on 15 Oct and $18.59 on 21 Oct. The deal was digested at roughly flat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public for two weeks and the stock round-tripped. What is unpriced is any 2027 outlook combining organic growth with the $25M of deal EBITDA (FY26 guide midpoint $122M). Financing question answered: the $75M cash buys a ~4x-EBITDA earnings stream, not distress, so the sign is non-negative.
evidence.independence: Terms and the $25M EBITDA / $200M RWP figures: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/porch-group-to-acquire-allied-trusts-insurance-carrier-and-mga/ (reporting the company's own release, same underlying document).

evidence.text: Expectations are high into the print. PRCH is +42% from the $12.36 close before the Q2 print to $17.59, -5% from its 52-week high, and near the ~$18.42 average analyst target. Q3 2025 was the same setup, with the stock up 68% and 22% on the two prior prints: a revenue and EBITDA beat with a raised guide fell 33.4% when the market focused on the net loss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 -33.4% on a beat after a large run. Q2 2026 +16.0% from a much lower base ($12.36, after a weak spring).
evidence.why_not_priced: The options market does not price this: skew is -6.3 vol points (upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.69, so the crowd is leaning long into the print. Short interest is 14.5% of shares outstanding with 9.3 days to cover, which can drive a squeeze. Much of it is likely convert-hedge, but it is still a reason to keep this negative small. Management has guided to positive FY net income, so last year's specific trigger (a net loss) is less likely.
